====Noun====
{{en-noun|s|been<l:dialectal>}}

# {{senseid|en|Q7391}}A [[fly]]ing [[insect]], of the [[clade]] {{taxfmt|Anthophila|clade}} within the [[hymenopteran]] superfamily {{taxfmt|Apoidea|superfamily}}, known for its organised societies (though only a minority have them), for collecting [[pollen]] and (in some species) producing [[wax]] and [[honey]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1499|author=w:John Skelton|title=The Bowge of Courte
|passage=His face was belymmed as '''byes''' had him stounge{{nb...}}.}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=III|canto=XII|text=An angry Wasp th'one in a viall had, / Th'other in hers an hony-laden '''Bee'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|book=II|chapter=12|passage=Can there be a more formall, and better ordered policie, divided into so severall charges and offices, more constantly entertained, and better maintained, than that of '''Bees'''?}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|act=V|scene=i|page=17|passage={{smallcaps|Ariell}}: / Where the '''Bee''' ſucks, there ſuck I, / In a Cowslips bell, I lie, / There I [[cowch]] when Owles doe crie, / On the Batts backe I doe flie / after Sommer merrily. / Merrily, merrily, ſhall I liue now / Vnder the bloſſom that hangs on the [[bough|Bow]].}}
#* {{RQ:Purchas Flying-Insects|chapter=The Excellency of Bees|page=1|passage='''Bees''' are the moſt excellent of all Inſects vvhatſoever, and expreſſe both vvorth and vvonder in all their vvaies: {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Lawrence Sons and Lovers|[[s:Sons and Lovers/Chapter 12|chapter 12]]|text=He stood across in the other garden, beside a bush of pale Michaelmas daisies, watching the last '''bees''' crawl into the hive.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2012-03-31|title=Subtle poison
|passage='''Bees''' pollinate many of the world’s crops—a service estimated to be worth $15 billion a year in America alone.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Jack Guy|title=Tiny QR codes help scientists track bee movements|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/28/science/bee-tracking-qr-codes-scli-intl/index.html|date=2025-01-28|passage=New insights into '''bee''' movements and life cycles have been uncovered after researchers tracked the insects using tiny QR codes glued onto their backs. {{...}} “This suggests that most of the foraging that the '''bees''' do occurs very close to the hive,” study co-author Margarita López-Uribe, an associate professor of entomology at PSU, told CNN on Monday.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250308001047/https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/28/science/bee-tracking-qr-codes-scli-intl/index.html}}
# {{lb|en|informal|proscribed}} Any stinging flying insect, especially a [[wasp]].

===Etymology 2===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₂-|id=speak}}
Possibly from dialectal {{m|en|bene}}, {{m|en|been}}, {{m|en|bean||help given by neighbours}}, from {{der|en|enm|been}}, {{m|enm|bene||neighbourly help, prayer, petition, request, extra service given by a tenant to his lord}},<ref>{{cite-web |title=Archived copy |titleurl=http://education.yahoo.com/reference/dictionary/entry/bee |accessdate=4 March 2012 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616030024/http://education.yahoo.com/reference/dictionary/entry/bee |archivedate=16 June 2012 }}</ref><ref>https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bee#word-history</ref> from {{der|en|ang|bēn||prayer, request, petition, favour, compulsory service}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*bōni}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bōniz||prayer, request, supplication}}. 

Thus a variant of obsolete {{m|en|ben||prayer; petition}} and {{doublet|en|boon|nocap=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|da|bøn||prayer}}, {{cog|nl|ban||curse}}, {{cog|de|Bann||ban}}. More at {{l|en|ban}}.

{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|contest}} A [[contest]], especially for [[spelling]]; see {{m|en|spelling bee}}.
#: {{co|en|geography '''bee'''}}
#* {{quote-av|en|title={{w|Clarence}}|date=24 July 2014|season=1|number=14|text=Hey, guys. Whoa. What are you guys doing? They're setting up in the gym for the Vision '''Bee'''. I signed our team up as "Sumo and the Laser Twins."|writer={{w|Spencer Rothbell}}|actor={{w|Tom Kenny}}|role=Sumo|time=7:02|episode=Puddle Eyes|publisher={{w|Cartoon Network Studios}}|}}
# {{senseid|en|gathering}} A community [[gathering]] to share labour, e.g. a sewing bee or a quilting bee.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1856|author=Samuel Griswold Goodrich|title=Recollections of a Lifetime
|passage=The cellar {{...}} was dug by a '''''bee''''' in a single day.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1973|author=Alan Skeoch; Tony H. Smith|title=Canadians and their society|page=139
|passage=There was but little variation in types of buildings in the pioneer period: house, church, store, barn and mill were usually much alike except in size, and a raising '''bee''' was the ordinary means of their erection.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Tim Blanning|title=The reinvention of the night|journal=Times Literary Supplement|date=21 Sep 2011
|passage=Particularly resistant, for example, in many parts of northern Europe was the “spinning '''bee'''”, a nocturnal gathering of women to exchange gossip, stories, refreshment and – crucially – light and heat, as they spun wool or flax, knitted or sewed.}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{der|en|fro|succeder}}, from {{uder|en|la|succedo|succedere|to go under, go from under, come under, approach, follow, take the place of, receive by succession, prosper, be successful}}.

Partly {{displaced|en|speed|nocap=1}}, of which the original sense “to succeed” only survives in a few {{lg|fossilized}} expressions such as {{m|en|Godspeed}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[follow]] something in [[sequence]] or [[time]].
#: {{ux|en|Autumn '''succeeds''' summer.}}
#* {{RQ:Browne Pseudodoxia Epidemica|edition=2nd|passage=Destructive effects {{...}} '''succeeded''' the curse.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[replace]] or [[supplant]] someone in order [[vis-à-vis]] an office, position,  or title.
#: {{synonyms|en|[[take]] the [[place]] of}}
#: {{ux|en|The king's eldest son '''succeeds''' his father on the throne.}}
#: {{ux|en|After a contentious election, Jones '''succeeded''' Smith as president of the republic.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To come after or follow; to be [[subsequent]] or [[consequent]]; {{q|often with ''to''}}.
#* {{RQ:Maugham Moon and Sixpence|[[s:The Moon and Sixpence/Chapter XLIX|chapter 49]]||Her arms were like legs of mutton, her breasts like giant cabbages; her face, broad and fleshy, gave you an impression of almost indecent nakedness, and [[vast]] chin '''succeeded''' to vast chin.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To come in the place of another person, thing, or event; to come [[next]] in the usual, natural, or [[prescribe]]d course of things; to follow; ''hence'', to come next in the possession of anything; {{q|often with ''to''}}.
#: {{syn|en|supersede|q1=formal}}
#: {{ux|en|Following the death of his mother, he '''succeeded''' to the throne.}}
#: {{ux|en|So, if the issue of the elder son '''succeed''' before the younger, the crown (or: property) falls to me.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1924|author=Faculty of Advocates (Scotland)|title=An Analytical Digest of Cases Decided in the Supreme Courts of Scotland, And, on Appeal, in the House of Lords, 1868 to 1922|page=159
|text=An heir in possession of an entailed estate '''succeeded''' to another estate under an entail which required him to denude of one of them. Held that before making his election he could not make up a title to or disentail the second estate.}}
## <!--or only chiefly intransitive?-->{{lb|en|intransitive}} To ascend the throne after the removal or death of the occupant.
##: {{ux|en|Princess Buttercup '''succeeded''' to the throne as queen after King Willoughby died.}}

|text=If he '''succeeded''' in February, 670, this would be his sixteenth year.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[prevail]] in [[obtaining]] an intended [[objective]] or [[accomplishment]]; to [[prosper]] as a result or conclusion of a particular effort.
#: {{ux|en|The persecution of any righteous practice has never '''succeeded''' in the face of history; in fact, it can expedite the collapse of the persecutory regime.}}
#: {{ux|en|She '''succeeded''' in her efforts to repair the tank.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2015-12-22|author=Amy E. Stich; Carrie Freie|title=The Working Classes and Higher Education: Inequality of Access, Opportunity and Outcome|publisher=Routledge|isbn=9781317444916
|text=Risk here refers to the fact that working-class families are less likely to have members who have already attended and '''succeeded''' at university, which means that university is perceived as a more uncertain and thus risky proposition.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To prosper or attain success and beneficial results in general.
#: {{ux|en|voted most likely to '''succeed'''}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1955|title=Soil Survey|page=35
|text=Legumes thrive better on this soil than on any of those derived entirely from acid materials. Applications of lime benefit clover {{...}} Even with artificial drainage, alfalfa will not '''succeed''', as roots cannot penetrate deep enough.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|dated}} To [[turn out]], [[fare]], [[do]] (well or ill).
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[support]]; to [[prosper]]; to [[promote]] or give success to.

#* {{quote-book|en|year=1666|author=Edward Stillingfleet|title=A Sermon preached before the honourable House of Commons ... October 10 ... third edition|page=31
|text={{...}} and his Royal Highness, who by their presence and incouragement inspired a new life and vigour into the sinking spirits of the Citizens, whereby God was pleased so far to '''succeed''' their endeavours, that a stop was put to the fury{{nb...}}}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[descend]], as an estate or an [[heirloom]], in the same family; to [[devolve]]; {{q|often with ''to''}}.

|text=A paterfamilias could arrange a marriage or emancipate a child without its mother's consent, and if the mother died intestate (possibly because her tutor refused to approve her will) her estate '''succeeded''' to her siblings, not to her husband or children, {{nb...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete|rare}} To fall [[heir]] to; to [[inherit]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1603|author=William Shakespeare|title=Measure for Measure
|passage=Else let my brother die, / If not a feodary, but only he / Owe and '''succeed''' thy weakness.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2019|author=D. Chandra Bose|title=Business Law, second edition|publisher=PHI Learning Pvt. Ltd.|isbn=9789387472242|page=314

# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete|rare}} To go down or near {{q|with ''to''}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1679|author=Edmund Spenser|title=The Works of that Famous English Poet, Mr. Edmond Spenser: Viz : The Faery Queen, [...] |page=293
|text=Who, ever as he saw him nigh '''succeed''', / Gan cry aloud with horrible affright, {{nb...}} }}
